items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: There was an elevated on 55th, elevated station, and I was right to the west of this elevated station at a place – I’m trying – this place had three or four big-time names. All the big-time horn players used to come to this place. It was upstairs, a gorgeous room. You had to go up some long stairs. I remember distinctly Coleman Hawkins playing there. I think Fletcher Henderson’s band played there. I used to practice all the time, like 20 hours a day. I was living over this great piano player. I didn’t know he was…

Prentice. So I’d be banging on this piano. Oh, I’d go nuts. My mother loved it. So she said, “Play, boy, play.” She’d be sitting on a chair. I’m just playing. Then finally I started playing the saxophone. He used to call up and say, “Please. Piano, maybe.” “But,” he said, “saxophone.” He said, “I can’t stand it. Stop.” The funny part about it was, years later, I got to play in this place myself, and guess who I hired?
